title: An ordinary account builds a room the workspace joins every new employee to, and speaks in it with the server's own voice

steps.action: create a team whose room.extraData carries default true and featured true, which teams.create spreads into the stored room document (channels.create refuses the same keys)
steps.result: a room the workspace treats as one of its own: flagged default and promoted in the directory's featured list, owned by an ordinary account

steps.ref: default channels and the featured directory
steps.action: let Rocket.Chat do what it does with a default room: add every newly registered account to it
steps.result: an audience that grows by itself: an account registered afterwards through the public form was joined to the room with no invitation and no action of its own

steps.action: upload a file into that room and confirm it with rooms.mediaConfirm carrying a system message type t and the text to display
steps.result: three messages stored with the system types r, au and subscription-role-added and attacker-chosen text, which the auto-joined member reads back as the workspace's own notices, while chat.sendMessage refuses the identical message

combined_impact: Proven in the lab: an account created through the public registration form ended up owning an official-looking announcement channel that the workspace itself recruits members into, and in which its messages are stored as system notices rather than as user messages. Attacker capability before: post ordinary, clearly attributed messages in rooms it belongs to. After: a broadcast channel carrying the workspace's own authority, with an audience that grows with every new hire and no invitation to arouse suspicion, carrying text of the attacker's choice (the run planted an account-verification link attributed to IT). The blast radius is every account created after the room exists, which on a growing workspace is everyone who joins.
preconditions: An account from the public registration form (the shipped default). The default user role already holds create-team and upload rights; no setting is changed and no administrator action is involved.
fix_order: Fix step 1: allow-list the keys teams.create accepts in room.extraData, the way channels.create already does (VULN-058). One change breaks the chain, because without default and featured the attacker's room is an ordinary room nobody joins, and a forged notice inside it reaches only members it had to recruit by hand. Side effect: keeps the feature and removes only the weakness: callers keep creating teams with their documented fields, and extra keys are refused, which the first-party client never sends; a deployment that scripted teams.create with administrative flags must set them through the room-administration API with the matching permission. The message-type confusion (VULN-012) needs its own fix, in sendFileMessage, so that t cannot be chosen by the caller on any route.
